clue.text: Hermit accepting university teacher's become capital fellow

indicators.note: the hermit accepts, taking the teacher into its middle

parts.note: a hermit lives alone: a loner
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A recluse who took in a college tutor has turned into a man about town.
explanation.walkthrough: The teacher goes between the third and fourth letters of the hermit word; ''s become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the capital city of Britain is a native or resident of it, a fellow of that city.

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the word before go mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper drops the nuts and the fruit from the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like food beside 'fruit', but it is the anagram signal on LOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloe is the small dark berry of the blackthorn, a kind of fruit used to flavour gin.

indicators.note: truncated means cut short, so the colour word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A cut-down set list from the band Green Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green Day' looks like the American punk band, but the two words are split and worked on separately.
explanation.definitionFit: When terms are set they are fixed and settled, just as agreed terms have been decided between parties.

clue.text: Con man disguised in dodgy tie

indicators.note: in places the first jumbled group inside the second
dodgy means unreliable or shifty, signalling these three letters are rearranged too
something disguised has its appearance altered, so these three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conman wearing a fake disguise and a dubious tie.
explanation.walkthrough: Each three-letter word is jumbled by its own signal, 'disguised' and 'dodgy'. 'Con' looks like a verb or a trickster but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Con is slang for a convict, a prisoner serving time in jail.

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes about, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lizard lies about on some boulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like stones the reptile sits among, but it is the anagram signal on IS AROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs were prehistoric reptiles, so one is an example of the class.

definitions.meaning: to be up for something, willing and ready, as in being up for a challenge
deer meat is wild hunted meat, the kind sold by poulterers alongside pheasant

explanation.surface: Cooked deer meat, served up.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ready for anything is a sporting idiom, and hunted wild animals as food carry the same word.

clue.text: Ruffian who loses head playing in goal

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its head
playing suggests the letters are in play, moving around into a new order

explanation.surface: A thug who gets his head knocked off while keeping goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' cuts WHO to HO; 'playing' turns IN GOAL into OLIGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruffian is a violent, rowdy troublemaker, the same as a thug or lout.

parts.note: to run a country is to govern it, so governed is ran

explanation.surface: A ruler boasts of having led a nation in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Persian Gulf country with Tehran as its capital, a state of the Middle East.

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: A notice telling you to post a poster on this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to something is to cling or be fastened to it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Make amends an hour after midday

definitions.meaning: to make up for a wrong or offence by way of reparation
1pm, the time reached sixty minutes past noon, read as two words

explanation.surface: An apology is due shortly after lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To make amends is to expiate a wrong, while the second sense is the clock time 1pm said as a phrase.

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer is a portion of the next word

explanation.surface: Wolf down a few of the sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: To gobble food is to consume it hurriedly and greedily.

clue.text: Where one might find glove available

definitions.meaning: a glove is worn on the end of the arm, so that is where it is found
ready and to hand, nearby for use

explanation.surface: A glove's whereabouts, and something within reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove sits literally at the end of one's arm, while the idiom means close by and ready to use.

indicators.note: puncturing means piercing, so the two letters go inside the friend word

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or pal
taken as its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Deflating a pal's ego with spiteful words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spleen' looks like the body organ, but here it is the old sense of bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen is old-fashioned for bitter anger and ill will, the same as bitterness of manner or speech.

clue.text: Coating of luxuriant hair receding — then finally none left

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, as a hairline does, so the hair word is read in reverse

parts.note: a mane is a thick flowing head of hair

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A man's flowing locks recede until nothing is left on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' turns MANE into ENAM; 'finally' takes the E ending 'none'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard glossy coating, on teeth or fired onto metal and pottery.

parts.note: a mission is an organised campaign or undertaking

explanation.surface: A political matter in a campaign across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to give out or discharge; emission is the noun for what is given out, here a noun synonym of issue.

clue.text: Thirsty person, perhaps, drinks River Test!

indicators.note: drinks means takes in, so the river letter goes inside the phrase for a thirsty person

parts.note: dry means thirsty
'un is colloquial for one, as in a young 'un, a person

explanation.surface: A parched soul takes a swig from a famous English trout river.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'dry 'un' is a thirsty person; 'drinks' sets R between the two parts. The River Test is a chalk stream in Hampshire, but 'Test' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal or trial run carried out before the real event is a practice test.

indicators.note: the tip is the point at the front, so the first letter of the next word

parts.note: an arrow is a projectile shot from a bow

explanation.surface: A slim, sharp Stone Age arrowhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow means thin or of small width, an adjective synonym for slender.

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: observed means saw
performed means did, as in did a turn

explanation.surface: Seeing a scandalous programme go out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns SAW into its sound-alike SOR, in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sordid is morally squalid and degrading, the kind of conduct one should be ashamed of.

clue.text: Road from outskirts of Stockport lined with oak, perhaps

indicators.note: lined with means having something inside, so the edge letters enclose the tree
the outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of the town's name

parts.note: an oak is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: A road leaving Stockport, a town near Manchester, is lined with oaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a public road in a town or city, lined with buildings.

explanation.surface: Giving a reply that is well suited.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt and appropriate both describe something suitable for the occasion.

clue.text: Classical writer's hero grotesquely seizing head of Medusa

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the jumbled letters enclose the next piece
grotesquely means in a distorted way, so the letters of the hero word are twisted
the head is the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An ancient poet's hero hideously grabs the Gorgon's severed head, as Perseus did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grotesquely' gives HOER from HERO; 'seizing' puts the M of Medusa inside. ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the ancient Greek epic poet of the Iliad and Odyssey, an author of classical antiquity.

clue.text: Feather duster harbours group of creatures

indicators.note: harbours means shelters within, so the answer sits inside the two words

explanation.surface: A feather duster gives shelter to a swarm of bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of animals, especially cattle or deer.

clue.text: Vegetable right next to a plate

parts.note: a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: A vegetable placed beside the plate on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crunchy red root vegetable, eaten raw in salads.

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A painter raised a single son.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish surrealist painter famed for melting clocks.

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: grind means hard repetitive toil

explanation.surface: Endless hard work somehow makes someone beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin is a broad smile, a near synonym.

parts.note: over means past, finished
a look is an appearance, how someone or something seems

explanation.surface: Ignore how someone used to look.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook a fault is to ignore or fail to notice it, a verb synonym of disregard.
